title: Tobacco cessation at work: How cotinine testing and health coaching support a healthier workforce
summary: See how employer benefits teams can use biometric screenings and cotinine testing to support smoking cessation, workforce health goals, and better business performance.
body_markdown:
Commercial tobacco use remains the[leading cause](https://www.cdc.gov/nccdphp/priorities/tobacco-use.html) of preventable disease and death in the U.S. For employers and their employees, the impact extends beyond individual health outcomes.


Tobacco use contributes to over[$240 billion in healthcare spending and approximately $185 billion](https://www.cdc.gov/nccdphp/priorities/tobacco-use.html) in lost productivity associated with smoking-related health conditions. For HR leaders and benefits decision-makers, those numbers carry real operational weight:


- Higher claims
- Longer absences
- Rising premiums that impact benefits budgets


Many organizations have responded by incorporating tobacco cessation programs into broader[workforce well-being strategies](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/articles/finding-right-balance-designing-health-benefits-work-employers-and-employees) since they’re one of the most direct levers available to address these issues. Smoking cessation benefits are now offered by an estimated[43% of smaller employers](https://files.kff.org/attachment/Employer-Health-Benefits-Survey-2025-Annual-Survey.pdf) (10-199 workers), with 68% of larger organizations (over 200) offering them, leaving substantial room for growth.


As employers continue to invest in population health initiatives, tobacco cessation has become an important component of[progressive biometric screening programs](https://www.labcorp.com/organizations/capabilities/employee-testing-wellness/biometric-screening) . Identifying tobacco users early, connecting them with meaningful resources, and tracking progress over time can support healthier employees while helping organizations manage healthcare costs, absenteeism, and productivity losses.


## **Industries where tobacco use runs highest**


While tobacco use affects every workforce, some industries continue to experience higher rates of tobacco use.[According to the CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/66/wr/mm6642a2.htm) , tobacco use is particularly common among workers in:


- Installation, maintenance, and repair occupations (37.2%)
- Construction (36.3%)
- Transportation and warehousing (32.8%)
- Mining (30.4%)
- Accommodation and food services (29.9%)
- Certain manufacturing environments (28.9%)


Not coincidentally, these industries often face elevated risks associated with chronic diseases such as[chronic obstructive pulmonary disease](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/articles/how-your-employees-can-quit-smoking-and-help-reduce-copd-risk) , cardiovascular conditions, and respiratory illnesses, as well as workplace injuries. They also frequently operate under physically demanding conditions where respiratory health, reaction time, and consistent attendance matter most.


For employers competing for talent in labor-intensive sectors, tobacco cessation programs in these environments don't just reduce claims but support workforce readiness, employee engagement, and long-term retention. Across all industries, tobacco cessation initiatives can contribute to a healthier workforce while supporting broader safety and wellness objectives.


## **Moving beyond traditional biometric screening programs**


Many employers already offer annual biometric screenings to help employees understand their health status better. Increasingly, organizations are expanding these programs to address lifestyle factors influencing long-term health outcomes.


The most effective employer wellness programs treat tobacco cessation as part of a broader, integrated approach to employee health, not a standalone offering. Cotinine, the primary metabolite of nicotine, serves as a reliable biomarker for tobacco use since it’s detectable for one to two days after nicotine use.


When cotinine testing is included in a biometric screening panel, employers gain objective, clinical confirmation of tobacco use alongside cholesterol, glucose, blood pressure, and other key health markers. This integration gives health coaches and program administrators a complete picture of employee health risk and offers employees a clear, supported pathway toward change.


Organizations commonly pair screening programs with incentives designed to encourage healthier behaviors. Depending on the program design, incentives may include:


- Cash rewards
- Premium discounts
- Tobacco-free wellness incentives
- Surcharges for employees who continue using tobacco products


In many cases, tobacco cessation coaching helps employees work toward healthier outcomes while maintaining access to incentives. When biometric screening programs include cotinine testing, employers gain greater visibility into tobacco use prevalence across their population and can more effectively connect employees to available resources.


The combination of objective testing, meaningful incentives, and accessible coaching consistently produces better program outcomes than incentives alone.


## **The increased value of point-of-care cotinine testing**


The good news is that the tools to act on these programs have never been more precise or more accessible at the point of care. Timely results can play an important role in employee engagement. Traditional lab-based testing remains an important option, but point-of-care testing introduces additional flexibility during on-site screening events.


Beginning in 2027, Labcorp plans to support tobacco cessation initiatives with a CLIA-waived oral fluid point-of-care cotinine test available through[WellConnect Plus](https://identityserver.wellconnectplus.com/account/login) ™ for on-site screening events. Designed to complement fingerstick screening events, the test delivers immediate results in as little as 10 minutes.


One of the most effective aspects of cotinine testing is its ability to connect employees with support at the right moment. The point-of-care approach offers several practical advantages:


- Immediate results during on-site events
- Faster access to information for your employees
- Simple oral fluid collection and testing procedures
- Consistent program administration across screening populations
- Integration with on-site events, including programs with dry blood spot testing
- Opportunities for timely engagement, education, cessation resources, and follow-up steps with a health coach


This approach can help streamline referrals into coaching programs, improve participation rates, and create a more cohesive experience between screening and intervention. Employees receive meaningful information about their health status, while employers gain a structured pathway for supporting positive behavior change.


## **Connecting cotinine test results to health coaching**


Identifying tobacco use is only the first step. Successful tobacco cessation strategies typically combine identification, education, behavioral support, and accountability.


When cotinine testing identifies tobacco use, connecting those employees to structured support facilitates the most impactful outcomes. Health coaching is commonly used for employees who test positive, giving them a concrete path to tobacco-free status while meeting HIPAA-compliant program design requirements. It can provide structured support, practical goal setting, and evidence-based behavior change strategies intended to help employees reduce or eliminate tobacco use.


Labcorp's Tobacco Cessation[Health Coaching](https://www.labcorp.com/organizations/capabilities/employee-testing-wellness/employee-health-coaching) program provides that bridge, offering employees access to certified coaches trained to support tobacco cessation through evidence-based approaches. In 2027, Labcorp will expand this capability with coaches holding Level 2 Tobacco Cessation Certifications through UMass Chan Medical School.


## **How to add cotinine testing to your 2027 on-site events**


Employers continue to face rising healthcare costs, ongoing productivity pressures, and increasing expectations around workforce well-being. Tobacco cessation initiatives address all three areas by helping employees reduce one of the most significant modifiable health risks.


As part of an enhanced biometric screening strategy, cotinine testing provides immediate, actionable insights supporting tobacco-free initiatives, wellness incentives, and targeted health coaching.
